title: R, reproducibility engineering and data management · Rung 1
subtitle: One dataset, one script, one command
coverLine: Keep the raw data untouched and let code do every change
subject: S52
author: Dr. Harsh Maheshwari

about.why: Most analyses that cannot be repeated were not wrong in their statistics. They were done by hand: a cell edited in a spreadsheet, a number pasted from a screen, a step nobody wrote down. This book teaches the opposite habit from the first line. You learn R as a language with objects, functions and packages, the tidyverse verbs that import, clean, summarise and plot a data frame, and one rule that makes the rest worth doing: raw data is never edited and every change lives in code that another person can run.
about.howToRead: Read Book 0 first, or at least the sections this book names as it goes. Then read this one in order, with R open beside it and every example typed, not pasted. The book asks you to build one thing: a single dataset analysed from raw file to final figure in one script that another person can run with one command. Start the script in the first section and extend it as you read.
about.prerequisites: Book 0, chiefly reading a table (F1), functions as input, rule and output (C4), average and spread (D5), graphs (C5, F2) and units (B1, B2, B6). The mathematics is Book 0’s arithmetic only: percentages, a mean and a median, and BMI as weight divided by height squared; nothing beyond it is used. No programming, no knowledge of files and folders and no statistics software is assumed; you need a computer on which you can install R and RStudio.

blurb: A short, practical book on starting data analysis the reproducible way. It covers R as a language, what a data frame is, the tidyverse verbs for importing, cleaning, summarising and plotting, why raw data is never edited and spreadsheets are never the place where analysis happens, and how to organise a project so that your whole analysis reruns from raw data with one command.
